dial.summary: The BOJ's September 18 hike (+25bps to 1.25%, a 31-year high) pulled DXY back below 100 into neutral territory—providing modest relief to TOTAL (recovering to $2.72T from a post-FOMC low of $2.67T)—but real yields at 2.65% (highest 10-year TIPS auction result since 2008) combined with the FOMC's September 16 hike to 3.75%–4.00% and hawkish dot plot keep Risk Off conditions firmly in place until real yields sustainably retreat below 2% or TOTAL establishes a new break above $2.8T.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) held at ~$103.5T as of September 2026 (MacroMicro/StreetStats latest G4 estimate; 6–8 week lag means July is the last month with full data); 4-week trend up confirmed (sustained upward direction since mid-August); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); broader global M2 (all major central banks) at a record ~$150T as of June 2026 per SpendNode; BOJ's September 18 hike (+25bps to 1.25%) will modestly affect yen-denominated G4 M2 components going forward but has no near-term impact on the reported aggregate.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1, below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down (Jul 55.6% → Aug 54.6% = −1.0pp); September ISM not released until October 1; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); FOMC Sep 16 hike to 3.75%–4.00% and BOJ Sep 18 hike to 1.25% add global financing-cost headwind; S&P Global Flash PMI Sep 23 is the next advance read.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY estimated ~99.8 on September 18, 2026, retreating from September 17's 100.07 close following the BOJ's +25bps hike to 1.25% (31-year high) which drove the yen to a 6.5-month high and pulled DXY to a 2-week low (down ~0.28% on the session); status now neutral (below 100 headwind threshold); 4-week trend flat: DXY was below 100 for the seven weeks preceding the FOMC's Sep 16 hike, briefly crossed above on Sep 16–17, and the BOJ Sep 18 returned it to sub-100 — net 4-week change from ~Aug 18 (~99.6) to Sep 18 (~99.8) ≈ +0.2%, below the 0.5% flat threshold; BOJ yen carry-trade unwind remains the primary near-term DXY downside catalyst.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS reopening auction on September 17, 2026 cleared at a real yield of 2.653% — the highest for this term since October 2008; FRED DFII10 secondary market cited at approximately 2.68% on Sep 16; using 2.65% as the auction-confirmed value; 4-week trend up: ~2.45% (Aug 18 estimate) → 2.65% (Sep 17) = +20bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% threshold both met); extreme real yield headwind remains the dominant macro drag on duration-sensitive risk assets; sustainably falling below 2% required to shift status.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 17–18, 2026: 10Y ~5.00%, 2Y ~4.73%, spread = +0.27% (+27bps); 4-week trend down (flattening): ~+38bps (Aug 18 estimate, pre-FOMC) → +27bps (Sep 17–18) = approximately −11bps, confirming 4-week flattening as the front-end 2Y repriced more aggressively than the long end following the FOMC's Sep 16 hike; status neutral (positive spread but not steepening on a 4-week basis; supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening; deeply inverted < −50bps for headwind does not apply); BOJ Sep 18 hike may cause mild global long-end repricing (steepening) but no confirmed Sep 18 close data yet.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.74T for week ending September 9, 2026 (H.4.1 released Sep 11, confirmed $6,740,619M); H.4.1 for week ending September 16 was released September 17 but not yet indexed — Sep 9 value carried forward; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 13) → $6.74T (Sep 9) = +$40B, within flat threshold; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no change to QT pace announced at Sep 16 FOMC); composition: $4,552B Treasuries, $1,914B MBS, $275B other.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate estimated at approximately +0.01% per 8h (Coinglass direct access unavailable due to network egress policy; carrying prior confirmed value); 30-day trend flat: near-zero throughout August–September 2026 as TOTAL declined from ~$2.75T to $2.67T post-FOMC and recovered to $2.72T following the BOJ Sep 18 hike; status supportive (near-zero confirms spot-driven price action, well below the 0.04% overheating threshold); BTC.D at 56.61% (eased from 57.0%), TOTAL at $2.72T; near-zero funding amid the post-FOMC correction confirms orderly deleveraging.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$306B (September 18, 2026; CoinGecko); total crypto market cap $2.72T (recovering from $2.67T post-FOMC low as BOJ Sep 18 hike weakened DXY below 100); stablecoin dominance 11.25% ($306B / $2.72T); 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% in early August 2026 → 11.25% (Sep 18) = approximately 2pp decline confirming net capital deployment into risk assets on the 30-day lens; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising dominance while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply as dominance fell from 11.5% to 11.25% even as TOTAL recovered to $2.72T); USDT leads at $183.4B (60.6%), USDC $74.2B; BTC.D at 56.61%.

upcoming.title: S&P Global Flash PMI (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: S&P Global US Flash PMI Composite, Manufacturing, and Services preliminary data for September 2026 at 9:45 AM ET — first advance September activity read capturing the full post-FOMC/BOE/BOJ tightening reaction (FOMC +25bps Sep 16, BOE hold Sep 17, BOJ +25bps Sep 18); leads ISM Manufacturing (Oct 1) and ISM Services; a sub-50 manufacturing reading would materially shift the November FOMC rate-path narrative.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 20, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 20, 2026 — labor market read in the first full week post-FOMC/BOE/BOJ tightening cluster; a sustained rise above 220K would signal early labor market cracks and shift October 27–28 FOMC rate expectations; prior weeks approximately 206K.

upcoming.title: Advance Durable Goods Orders (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Durable Goods Orders for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — watch non-defense capital goods ex-aircraft (key business investment proxy for Q3 GDP); elevated borrowing costs (10Y ~5%) and DXY returning to neutral territory weigh on capex decisions; ISM Manufacturing new orders fell to 53.7 in August (−3.0pp); Q2 2026 GDP third estimate follows September 30.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Final)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers final September 2026 reading at 10:00 AM ET — first final sentiment read fully capturing the post-FOMC (Sep 16), BOE hold (Sep 17), and BOJ hike (Sep 18) trifecta; year-ahead inflation expectations closely watched by the Fed; a sharp drop in current conditions or spike in inflation expectations could shift November FOMC positioning; released same day as Advance Durable Goods.
